title: Smoke Detector Battery
repairSteps: Twist the detector unit counter-clockwise to remove it from the ceiling mount.
Open the battery compartment on the back of the unit.
Remove the old 9V battery and insert the new one, ensuring correct polarity.
Press and hold the 'Test' button for 5 seconds to confirm functionality.
Twist the unit back into the ceiling mount.
notes: Test alarms monthly and replace the whole alarm every 10 years. Check all other detectors in the house while the ladder is out.

title: Dishwasher Filter
repairSteps: Pull out the bottom dish rack completely.
Rotate the cylindrical filter lock to the 'Unlock' position.
Lift the filter assembly out of the dishwasher floor.
Clean the filter under running water with soap and a soft brush to remove debris.
Reinsert the filter and twist to lock it back into place.
notes: Clean more frequently if running heavy-duty cycles with high food residue.

title: Refrigerator Water Filter
repairSteps: Turn off the water supply to the refrigerator.
Open the filter cover (its location varies by model; check the user manual).
Rotate the old filter counter-clockwise to unlock and remove it.
Remove the protective cap from the new filter and insert it.
Twist the new filter clockwise until it locks, aligning the lock symbol with the indicator line.
Turn the water supply back on.
notes: Dispense water after replacement to clear air from the line. Replace sooner if dispensing slows.

title: Dryer Vent Cleaning
repairSteps: Unplug the dryer, then disconnect the flexible duct from the back of the dryer.
Insert the vent brush into the duct and run it through to the exterior exit.
Vacuum out the lint collected at the dryer end.
Clear any debris from the exterior vent flap.
Reconnect the duct and plug the dryer back in.
notes: Crucial for fire prevention; clean sooner if clothes take longer than usual to dry, and check for kinks in the hose.

title: Sump Pump Test
repairSteps: Slowly pour water into the sump pit until the float switch is triggered.
Ensure the pump activates immediately and evacuates the water.
Check the discharge pipe outside to ensure water is flowing away from the foundation.
notes: Test each season, including before the spring rainy season.

title: Water Softener Salt
repairSteps: Lift the lid of the brine tank.
Check the salt level; refill if the tank is less than half full.
Pour in the salt pellets; the average household uses about two bags every two months.
Close and secure the lid.
notes: Use water softener salt rather than rock salt, which leaves insoluble residue in the brine tank.

title: HVAC Condenser Coil Cleaning
repairSteps: Turn off the power to the AC unit at the outdoor disconnect box.
Remove any leaves or debris from around the unit.
Use a soft brush to gently remove dust from the fins.
Spray the coils with a garden hose (low pressure) from the inside out.
notes: Do not use a pressure washer as it will bend the aluminum fins.

title: Fire Extinguisher Inspection
repairSteps: Check the pressure gauge to ensure the needle is in the green zone.
Verify the safety pin is intact and the seal is not broken.
Look for leaks, dents, or corrosion on the canister.
Check the expiration date on the label.
notes: If the gauge is outside the green zone, have the unit serviced or replaced. Your local fire department can advise where.

title: Gutter Cleaning
repairSteps: Set up the ladder on stable ground.
Scoop out organic debris and leaves from the gutters.
Flush the gutters with a hose to ensure downspouts are clear.
Inspect for leaks or sagging sections.
notes: Safety first: Always have a spotter when using extension ladders.

title: Toilet Flapper Replacement
repairSteps: Shut off the water supply valve behind the toilet.
Flush the toilet to empty the tank.
Unhook the flapper chain from the flush lever.
Unhook both flapper ears from the arms on the flush valve.
Clean any sediment or debris from the flush valve opening.
Hook the new flapper's ears onto the arms and attach the chain, leaving one to two links of slack.
Turn the water supply back on.
notes: Prevents 'phantom flushing' and saves water. Check for silent leaks yearly: add food coloring to the tank, wait 10 minutes, and look for color in the bowl.

title: Vacuum Filter Wash
repairSteps: Remove the filter from the vacuum assembly.
Rinse under cold water until the water runs clear.
Tap the filter gently to remove excess water.
Allow to air dry for at least 24 hours, until completely dry, before reinstalling.
notes: Do not use detergent or put the filter in a dishwasher or washing machine.

title: Smart Lock Battery Change
repairSteps: Remove the battery cover from the interior side of the lock.
Remove the two old CR123A batteries.
Insert two new CR123A lithium batteries, ensuring correct polarity.
Replace the cover and test the lock via the app.
notes: Change batteries immediately when the app warns 'Low Battery'. Operate the lock three times from the app afterward to clear the alert.

title: Refrigerator Coil Dusting
repairSteps: Pull the refrigerator away from the wall.
Unplug the unit from the power outlet.
Vacuum the dust and pet hair from the condenser coils at the back/bottom.
Push the refrigerator back into place and plug it in.
notes: Dusty coils force the compressor to work harder, increasing electricity bills.

title: Door Hinge Lubrication
repairSteps: Apply a small amount of silicone lubricant to the hinge pin.
Open and close the door several times to distribute the oil.
Wipe away any excess lubricant with a paper towel to prevent staining.
notes: Use silicone spray rather than standard WD-40 for longer-lasting results.

title: Water Heater Flush
repairSteps: Turn off the electricity and the cold water inlet.
Connect a garden hose to the drain valve and lead it somewhere hot water won't cause damage.
Open the pressure relief valve, then open the drain valve and drain the tank completely.
Close the drain valve, disconnect the hose, and close the pressure relief valve.
Turn on all hot water faucets and open the cold water inlet to refill the tank.
Once water flows from each faucet, turn it off, then turn the electricity back on.
notes: Removes sediment buildup to improve heating efficiency. Flush every 6 months if you have hard water.
